reaction.notes:
Use this file ONLY if 'applies_if' tokens are present.
Then try base_rules (top→down). If none match, use default_rule.
After picking a rule, scan all modifiers and apply those that match (tokens OR plain‑text heuristics).
Notes: prefer Oxyma (vs HOBt/HOAt) for safety and lower epimerization. Minimize pre‑activation time for α‑chiral acids. Avoid catalytic DMAP when α‑stereocenters are present. For difficult pairs, consider acyl fluoride or acid chloride routes with strict temperature control.

applies_if.expr: (Any-CO2H OR Ar-CO2H OR Arom-CO2H OR Vinyl-CO2H OR Any-COCl OR Ar-COCl OR Arom-COCl) AND (Any-NH2 OR Ar-NH2 OR Arom-NH2 OR Bn-NH2 OR Allyl-NH2 OR Vinyl-NH2 OR Any-NHR OR Ar-NHR OR Arom-NHR OR Bn-NHR OR Allyl-NHR)

default_rule.description: General amidation via EDCI + Oxyma under mild basic conditions (low epimerization).

conditions.order_of_addition: Acid + Oxyma + base (cold, 5–10 min) → add EDCI (brief pre‑activation) → add amine
conditions.notes: Use Oxyma to suppress N‑acylurea/O→N acyl transfer. Avoid long pre‑activation.

conditions.coupling_system: EDCI + Oxyma (preferred); alt: T3P or DMTMM; alt2: TFFH (acyl fluoride)
conditions.notes: Avoid DMAP. For very hindered cases but still chiral, consider acyl fluoride (TFFH) at 0–5 °C.

base_rules.name: Sterically hindered pairs / poor nucleophiles
base_rules.description: Fast, strong activators; escalate if sluggish.

conditions.notes: Short pre‑activation (≤5–10 min). If still slow, escalate to acyl chloride or acyl fluoride route (see BR_acyl_halide_like).

conditions.coupling_system: HATU or COMU + DIPEA; optional catalytic DMAP 5–10 mol% if no α‑stereocenter
conditions.notes: If α‑chiral acid: omit DMAP and run ≤10 °C with brief activation.

base_rules.name: Acid‑ or base‑sensitive functionality
base_rules.description: Neutral/mild profiles to protect sensitive motifs.

conditions.coupling_system: CDI (acyl imidazole) then amine; alt: DMTMM (mild, often no added base)
conditions.stoichiometry_equiv: CDI 1.1–1.5 eq (pre‑form acyl imidazole), then amine 1.2 eq; optional base 1–2 eq
conditions.solvent: THF or DMF (for CDI); MeOH/MeCN/H2O mixes for DMTMM
conditions.notes: CO₂ evolution with CDI; neutral to mildly basic conditions. Good chemoselectivity with DMTMM.

base_rules.name: Aqueous / bioconjugation‑leaning or late‑stage
base_rules.description: Buffered or wet media; amide over ester selectivity.

conditions.coupling_system: EDCI + Oxyma or NHS in buffered aqueous‑organic (pH 5–6); alt: DMTMM in MeOH/H₂O
conditions.stoichiometry_equiv: Acid 1.00, Amine 1.2, EDCI 1.2–1.5, Oxyma/NHS 1.1–1.5, Buffer to pH 5–6
conditions.solvent: H₂O/MeCN or H₂O/DMF; for DMTMM: MeOH/H₂O
conditions.notes: pH control critical. Adjust buffer to bias amide formation.

conditions.coupling_system: T3P (50% in EtOAc) ± base; alt: DIC + Oxyma (filter DCU)
conditions.stoichiometry_equiv: Acid 1.00, Amine 1.2, T3P (50%) 1.5–2.0; optional base 0–2 eq
conditions.notes: T3P gives water‑soluble phosphate residues; DCU from DIC can be filtered.

base_rules.name: Very hindered acids or especially weak amines
base_rules.description: Escalation to acyl halide/fluoride with strict temp control.

conditions.coupling_system: Acid chloride (SOCl2/oxalyl chloride, cat. DMF) or acyl fluoride (TFFH) → amine + base
conditions.stoichiometry_equiv: Acid 1.00 → acyl halide; then Amine 1.2, base (Et3N or 2,6‑lutidine) 2–3
conditions.solvent: DCM or toluene for halide formation; then DCM/THF
conditions.notes: Highest racemization risk—avoid for α‑chiral acids unless essential; prefer acyl fluoride over chloride when possible.

conditions.coupling_system: Mixed anhydride via IBCF + DIPEA (−20→0 °C) → add amine
conditions.notes: Lower epimerization than acid chlorides; maintain low temp.

modifiers.suggest: Use Oxyma (vs HOBt/HOAt) for safety and to suppress O→N acyl transfer and N‑acylurea formation.
Avoid catalytic DMAP; it can increase epimerization. Keep activation cold and brief.
Limit pre‑activation to ≤5–10 min at 0–10 °C; add amine promptly.
Favor MeCN/DMF; avoid strongly apolar media for ionic coupling systems.
Consider acyl fluoride (TFFH) at 0–5 °C for hindered substrates with better control vs acid chlorides.
Add 5–10 mol% DMAP to accelerate anilide formation; omit if α‑stereocenter exists.
If DCC used, filter DCU (hot or wet) and rinse thoroughly to avoid occlusion.
Wash with aq. bicarbonate and brine to remove phosphorous residues from T3P.
Verify ee after coupling (e.g., chiral HPLC or Mosher amide analysis) on a small‑scale scout run.
Increase temperature stepwise (e.g., +10–20 °C) or switch to a stronger activation system.
Use anhydrous solvents and fresh base; avoid aqueous buffers unless specifically chosen (DMTMM/EDCI buffered routes).
Prefer 2‑MeTHF or EtOAc when compatible; avoid chlorinated solvents unless necessary for acyl halide formation.
